events.title: Golden Spike Completes the First Transcontinental Railroad
events.description: At Promontory Summit, Utah Territory, a ceremonial golden spike was driven to join the Central Pacific and Union Pacific railroads, linking the eastern and western rail networks of the United States.
events.significance: Cross-country travel fell from months to about a week, which accelerated westward settlement, commerce, and national economic integration.

events.title: Germany Invades the Low Countries and Churchill Becomes Prime Minister
events.description: Germany launched its offensive against France by invading the Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg. On the same day, Neville Chamberlain resigned and Winston Churchill became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
events.significance: The invasion opened the Battle of France and the western phase of World War II in earnest, while Churchill's leadership shaped Britain's determination to keep fighting.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Inaugurated as President of South Africa
events.description: Nelson Mandela was sworn in as South Africa's first Black president following the country's first multiracial democratic elections, ending the formal apartheid system.
events.significance: The inauguration marked the end of decades of institutionalized racial segregation and the start of a democratic, multiracial South Africa.

events.title: Louis XVI Becomes King of France
events.description: Louis XVI ascended the French throne upon the death of his grandfather, Louis XV, at the age of 19.
events.significance: His reign saw severe financial crisis and the outbreak of the French Revolution in 1789, which ended the monarchy and transformed Europe.

events.title: Rudolf Hess Flies to Scotland
events.description: Deputy Führer Rudolf Hess made a solo flight to Scotland, where he parachuted near Glasgow, apparently hoping to negotiate peace with Britain. He was arrested and held as a prisoner for the rest of the war.
events.significance: The bizarre episode embarrassed the Nazi leadership and remains one of the most debated mysteries of World War II.
